 Women's College Basketball Rankings: AP Poll Top 25 released after Week 1
 Nick Schultz @ NickSchultz_7 2h 0 Share Share 
 Through the first week of the women’s college basketball season, a top-five matchup delivered. That also led to some movement in the rankings, based on the latest AP Top 25 poll released Monday morning.
 UConn and Michigan squared off on Thursday, and the Wolverines came away with the victory over the No. 2-ranked Huskies in Ann Arbor. Olivia Olson and Te’Yala Delfosse led the charge offensively in the effort.

 As a result, there was a shakeup at the top of the latest AP Top 25 , but the No. 1 team remained the same in the women’s college basketball rankings. Here is the full poll following the opening week of the 2026-27 season.
 1. South Carolina (-)
 After starting the year with an eight-point win over Maryland, South Carolina didn’t leave room for doubt in a Top-15 matchup against North Carolina. It was all Gamecocks as they got an 84-39 win over the Tar Heels at home.

 South Carolina remains atop the AP Top 25 after Week 1 following the performance. This will be a big week, though, as the Gamecocks get ready to take on USC in Greenville for a Sunday matinee Nov. 15 on ABC.
 2. Michigan (+3)
 In its season opener, Michigan picked up a signature victory. The Wolverines took down No. 2 UConn at Crisler Center in a top-five affair and jumped up to that No. 2 ranking in the latest AP Top 25.
 Te’Yala Delfosse had 22 points and nine rebounds while Olivia Olson had 19 points, eight rebounds, four assists and four steals. Michigan then cruised past Wright State in the following game in Week 1.
 3. USC (-)
 USC put up at least 100 points in each of its first two games to start the 2026-27 season, including a victory over UNLV in Las Vegas. It was also the first look at the duo of Jazzy Davidson and JuJu Watkins together on the court.
 So far, so good as USC picked up a 100-68 win over UNLV and a 118-40 win over Utah State. After Tuesday’s game against Charleston, the Trojans will head to Greenville, South Carolina for a showdown with top-ranked South Carolina.
 4. UConn (-2)
 In UConn’s second game of the season, the Huskies struggled with ball control against Michigan. They turned it over 19 times in the loss to the Wolverines, but got a bounce-back victory over No. 10 Iowa to stay toward the top of the AP Top 25.
 Sarah Strong is off to an impressive start to the season, averaging 23.7 points and 7.3 rebounds. Jovana Popovic is also averaging 18 points through the first three games of the 2026-27 season.
 5. Duke (-1)
 Duke got the year started with two double-digit victories out of the gate. The Blue Devils stayed in the Top 25 of the AP Top 25 after the opening week of the season as they continue to go through the non-conference schedule.
 Through the first few games, Duke has used a balanced scoring attack. Arianna Robinson and Aaliyah Crump averaged 12 points across the opening week, with Crump leading the team with 4.0 assists and 1.5 steals, and Robinson averaging 3.0 blocks.
 6. Texas (-)
 Texas started out its season in grand fashion with back-to-back blowout victories. The Longhorns haven’t left any room for doubt to start the year and remain one of the top teams in the country after Week 1.
 Madison Booker put up 30 points in the opener against Northern Colorado and 24 points against Fairleigh Dickinson to get her senior year underway. Texas was one of the favorites in the SEC preseason poll this year and so far, it’s been an impressive start.
 7. Louisville (-)
 After entering Week 1 as a Top-10 team, Louisville cruised through its first three games. The Cardinals took down Bellarmine, Stetson and Southern Indiana out of the gate to get things underway.
 Louisville has a big non-conference matchup coming up Nov. 15, though. The Cardinals will welcome UConn to the KFC Yum! Center for a Top-10 battle that will be one of the biggest games of the early part of the season.
 8. Vanderbilt (-)
 Across its first two games of the year, Vanderbilt showcased its offense. The Commodores scored 100 points in each of their opening games and stayed squarely in the Top 10 after the opening week.
 Vanderbilt took down Lipscomb 112-53 and Queens 100-42 out of the gate. Following games against Morehead State and Western Kentucky, the Commodores will play a neutral-site game against Iowa as part of a huge Sunday slate.
 9. LSU (-)
 LSU flexed its muscle in a big way across its opening games of the season. The Tigers scored 129 points in the opener and 131 points in Game 2 as part of a dominant start to the year, and they remain a Top-10 team in the AP Top 25.
 LSU defeated Southeast Louisiana 129-35 on opening night and then flew past Texas Southern 131-22 on Thursday. ZaKiyah Johnson led the charge with a team-high 25 points per game through the opening week.
 T-10. UCLA (+1)
 After losing multiple pieces of last year’s title team, UCLA’s new-look roster got off to a strong start this season. The Bruins took down Lehigh and UC Irvine convincingly out of the gate to get things underway.
 Sienna Betts, one of the returning members from last year’s group, is averaging 16 points through the opening week. She is expected to be one of the leaders for UCLA this year, and the Bruins will now get ready to take on Arizona.
 T-10. Iowa (-)
 After resounding wins over Towson and Eastern Illinois to start the year, Iowa struggled to contain Sarah Strong in Sunday’s loss to UConn. Still, the Hawkeyes remain in the Top 10 of the AP Top 25 through Week 1.
 Chit-Chat Wright had a team-high 23 points against UConn while Amari Whiting had 10 points and seven rebounds in the effort. Iowa will now get ready to square off against UNI on Thursday before a neutral-site bout with Vanderbilt.
 12. Kentucky (+2)
 Kentucky began the opening week with a 3-0 record, including a ranked victory over No. 25 NC State. Ajsa Sivka and Clara Strack have led the charge through the early part of the year for Kenny Brooks’ group.
 Sivka dropped 32 points in the victory over NC State, her third college game after she was cleared to play this year despite being drafted by the Chicago Sky. She did not sign a WNBA contract. UK is looking to be squarely in the mix in a loaded SEC race this year, and the non-conference schedule continues Wednesday against Evansville.
 13. Notre Dame (-)
 It was a strong start to the year for Notre Dame, which took down Villanova in Rome as part of the 2026-27 season opener. The Irish followed that up with a blowout victory over Stonehill to get things underway.
 Hannah Hidalgo remains one of the nation’s top playmakers as she put up 29.5 points, 5.0 assists and 6.5 steals across the first two games. Leah Macy is also emerging as a key player for Notre Dame with 25.5 points and 11 rebounds through the opening week.
 14. Oklahoma (+7)
 It would’ve been tough to draw up a better start for Oklahoma, which took down North Carolina in its opening game. The Sooners are sure to be in the mix for the SEC this year and were one of the biggest movers in the AP Top 25.
 LeeLee Bell led the way for OU through its first two games with 22.5 points, 10.0 rebounds and 2.5 steals on average. That includes 25 points and eight rebounds in the 91-79 victory over North Carolina in the season opener.
 15. TCU (-)
 Through the opening week, TCU got three resounding victories to start the 2026-27 season. The Horned Frogs remain squarely in the AP Top 25 heading into the second week of the year, as well.
 TCU put up at least 89 points in each of its first three games and did not allow more than 43 points in the process. The Horned Frogs entered the year as the No. 15 team in the women’s college basketball rankings and remain right in the middle of the latest Top 25.
 16. Washington (-)
 Washington started the year 2-0 in big fashion with back-to-back blowout victories over UC San Diego and Pacific. While the non-conference schedule will ramp up a bit in the coming weeks, it was still an impressive start for the Huskies.
 Salvia Sellers put up 21 points and 8.5 assists across the first two games while Avery Howell averaged 18.5 points through Week 1. Next time out, Washington will take on Bakersfield on Tuesday before visiting Washington State for the rivalry matchup.
 17. Ohio State (+1)
 Ohio State did not leave any doubt in Week 1, cruising to a 3-0 start. That includes a 103-36 victory over Central Michigan in the second game of the year as the Buckeyes remained in the middle of the AP Top 25.
 Jaloni Cambridge put up 20.7 points per game through the first three games of the season while Elsa Lemmila had 16.3 points and 9.0 rebounds out of the gate. Ohio State has a marquee matchup looming Thursday, though, as UConn comes to Columbus for a battle on FS1.
 18. Minnesota (-1)
 Minnesota picked up a key power conference victory in Week 1 with a road win over Marquette. The Golden Gophers got a strong performance from Grace Grocholski in the effort and remain squarely in the AP women’s basketball Top 25 poll.
 Grocholski had 25 points, including five three-pointers, to go with 11 rebounds to lead the charge. Minnesota will now get ready to face Southern before taking on Kansas State on Saturday afternoon.
 T-19. Oklahoma State (+3)
 Oklahoma State did not allow 40 points to either opponent in its first two games of the season. The Cowgirls’ defensive effort was on full display against both Southern and Morgan State to start things off.
 New addition Audi Crooks has looked the part through the first week of the season with a team-high 18 points and 9.0 rebounds. She was the biggest addition for the Cowgirls this offseason and had a double-double in that win over Morgan State.
 T-19. Maryland (+1)
 Despite the season-opening loss to South Carolina on opening day, Maryland remains in the AP Top 25 after Week 1. The Terrapins began the year ranked at No. 20 before the 1-1 start in the first week.
 Maryland kept things close against South Carolina in Paris to start the season while suffering the 101-93 loss. UMD then bounced back with a victory over George Mason to get back in the win column.
 21. Ole Miss (-2)
 Ole Miss cruised to a 2-0 start to the season with victories over Alcorn State and North Alabama in Week 1. The Rebels are predicted to be in the middle of the SEC race once again this year and held strong in the AP Top 25, as well.
 Ole Miss got big games from Jaida Civil and Jada Richard to start the 2026-27 season. Games against UAlbany and Louisiana Tech are next up this week before the Rebels visit Ohio State on Nov. 18.
 22. Illinois (+1)
 Illinois started off the season in a big way with resounding wins over Detroit Mercy and Southern. The Fighting Illini entered the year ranked No. 23 in the AP Top 25 and remain squarely in the poll after Week 1.
 Cearah Parchment is putting up 20 points per game across the opening week while Berry Wallace is putting up 17 points and 8.0 rebounds per game. Illinois will continue non-conference play Nov. 15 against SEMO before taking on Ball State.
 23. North Carolina (-11)
 North Carolina didn’t shy away with its start to the season, facing off against two ranked opponents. The Tar Heels dropped both games to Oklahoma and South Carolina, but remained in the AP Top 25 after Week 1.
 UNC fell to Oklahoma 91-79 in Paris to start the year before struggling mightily against South Carolina in Charlotte. The Tar Heels will now return home to take on NC Central as they seek their first win of the season.
 24. West Virginia (-)
 West Virginia is off to a 3-0 start, including a victory over Georgia Tech, to stay in the AP Top 25 after Week 1. The Mountaineers got big performances from Skylar Forbes and Gia Cooke as part of that victory over the Yellow Jackets.
 WVU was predicted to finish fourth in the Big 12 preseason poll and received a first-place vote, as well. The Mountaineers will now get ready to take on Northwestern this week as part of the non-conference slate.
 25. Nebraska (+1)
 With two resounding victories to start the year, Nebraska is now in the AP Top 25 after Week 1. The Cornhuskers cruised past San Jose State and Western Illinois to get things underway and move into the rankings.
 NU was one of the teams that received votes last week before the strong start. Britt Prince was a big part of the strong start with 21 points, 3.5 assists and 2.5 steals through the opening matchups.
 Others receiving votes: Baylor 39, NC State 35, Arizona State 20, Virginia 18, Kansas 8, Florida 4, Michigan State 3, Fairfield 2, Colorado 2, Tennessee 1, Princeton 1
